claims.text: The as-cast HfNbTaTiZr alloy is a fully random BCC solid solution.
Annealing HfNbTaTiZr at 1000 °C for 24 h followed by quenching induces and retains chemical short-range order.
An annealing temperature of 1000 °C is approximately 0.5 Tm for HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed CSRO consists of clustered Hf–Ta and Nb–Zr enrichments.
Diffuse-scattering XRD or atom-probe tomography can be used to determine the degree of CSRO.
CSRO reduces local lattice distortions in HfNbTaTiZr.
CSRO reduces anharmonic vibrational amplitudes in HfNbTaTiZr.
CSRO strengthens local bonds and increases local bond stiffness.
The CSRO-induced changes impede dislocation glide and climb at elevated temperature.
Impeded dislocation motion raises the elevated-temperature yield strength.
Reduced lattice anharmonicity lowers thermal lattice expansion and the coefficient of thermal expansion.
Increased local bond stiffness increases the elastic modulus.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, the annealed alloy will exhibit a 10–20% increase in yield strength at 800 °C.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, the annealed alloy will exhibit an approximately 5% decrease in average CTE over 300–900 °C.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, the annealed alloy will exhibit an approximately 5% higher elastic modulus at 600 °C.
The CSRO-based mechanism is expected to hold only up to approximately 0.5 Tm, identified as about 900 °C.
Above about 900 °C, long-range ordering or phase separation may invalidate the CSRO-based mechanism.
The comparison should use as-cast and 1000 °C/24 h annealed HfNbTaTiZr specimens tested under otherwise identical conditions.
Compression should be conducted from 300–900 °C at approximately 10^-3 s^-1, with dilatometry and resonant ultrasound from 300–900 °C in inert atmosphere.
The hypothesis is falsified if confirmed CSRO produces no statistically significant change greater than 3% in the specified yield-strength, CTE, or elastic-modulus comparisons.

contradictions.description: The intervention labels 1000 °C as approximately 0.5 Tm, whereas the boundary labels approximately 900 °C as 0.5 Tm.
